title: Fuzzing in the GenAI Era — Leonard Tang, Haize Labs
talk_summary: Haize Labs argues that static golden-dataset evals miss LLM brittleness (sensitivity to small input perturbations), so they run iterative fuzz/optimization loops: generate stimuli, score outputs with a judge, use the score to guide the next search until bugs are found or budget is exhausted. Their key practical claim is that judge quality can be scaled cheaply by building agentic judges (debate, self-verification, ensembling, rubric fan-out) on small models rather than calling frontier models.

takeaways.technique: Agentic judge instead of single LLM call
takeaways.what_they_do: Replace one-shot LLM-as-judge with a pipeline of primitives: rubric fan-out (propose per-item criteria), self-verification, debate between weaker models, and ensembling, then aggregate.
takeaways.numbers: Verdict on GPT-4o-mini backbone beats o1/o3-mini/GPT-4/3.5-Sonnet on expert QA verification at <1/3 the cost and <1/3 the latency

takeaways.what_they_do: Treat input generation as discrete optimization: generate stimuli, score outputs with the judge, feed the score back to guide the next round of search, iterate until bugs found or budget exhausted.
Have the judge first propose data-point-specific criteria (like unit tests for that input), then critique the output against each criterion, rather than applying one global rubric.
takeaways.numbers: GRPO-tuned 1.7B model reached 80.7% on RewardBench, competitive with Claude 3 Opus (~80%) and GPT-4o-mini (~80%)

takeaways.technique: Stack small models with more judge-time compute
takeaways.what_they_do: Deliberately use a cheap backbone model and spend extra inference calls on structured judging (debate/self-verify/ensemble) to beat a single frontier call.
takeaways.numbers: beats o1 at <1/3 cost and <1/3 latency

takeaways.what_they_do: Before trusting a judge, validate it against human ground truth and treat judge instability (order bias, rubric sensitivity, uncalibrated scales) as a first-class failure mode to measure.
takeaways.numbers: 38% increase in ground-truth human agreement using Verdict vs internal ops teams

takeaways.technique: Adversarial input emulation for user-facing agents
takeaways.what_they_do: Run an optimization-driven adversary against user-facing apps to find prompt injections, jailbreaks, and unhandled corner cases before production.
takeaways.numbers: work that took a team ~3 months took ~5 minutes on their platform (their claim)
